answer: Each season the fishermen weave new wicker baskets for the weir and the catch is weighed against the weir book, and only a weighed catch may be sold at market. A jade basket woven from stolen withies fails the count: at the opal of the weir the weave must match the fishermen's own pattern, and a strange basket catches nothing. Forging the catch means weaving baskets for a season, bribing a fisherman and paying 7,400, while the shale tally in the weir book is read at every market day, so a catch whose baskets were never counted is thrown back into the river.
